guard: the holder starts at most one emitter for the path it binds, and later callers get the one that already exists rather than a second start
why: START-ONCE IS HELD BY TWO REDUNDANT THINGS AND THAT IS WHY IT WENT UNREGISTERED FOR SO LONG.
The `boundPath` gate is what actually stops a second `startEmitter`: it is set before the await,
so a later call for the same path never takes that arm again. The `this.emitter` shortcut and the
trailing `return this.emitter` answer for each other, so breaking either one alone changes nothing
this suite can see. Six single-site mutations were measured and all six survived at 33 passed,
0 failed. The suite header carries that table.
THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM THAT TABLE WAS WRONG, AND THIS FILE IS THE CORRECTION. It said no
registration was possible, because `scripts/mutation-proof.mjs` takes one find and one replace per
mutation. That reasoning treated `single find/replace` as `single site`, and the two sites here are
ADJACENT: one contiguous span covers the shortcut and the gate together, which is a legal mutation
and kills. A reviewer proved it with the shipped tool rather than arguing it. An impossibility
claimed about a property that DOES have a kill is exactly the defect class this branch exists for,
so the kill is registered instead of an accepted-gap sentence.
BLAST RADIUS IS TWO AND IT IS STATED. H1 reds both `lazy:` cells, not only the one `expectRed`
names. A mutant that reddens its named cell plus others is neither a clean pass nor a failure; it
carries the count so a later reader is not surprised by the second name.
THE ANCHOR IS PURE CODE. It spans no comment, so a rewording of the prose around it cannot turn
this mutant into a no-op the way an edit to the halt message did to S26 in this same branch.

mutations.name: H1 both start-once guards removed in one contiguous span, because they are adjacent and one find covers them
mutations.note: Removing either guard alone survives, because the other answers for it. Removed together, a second adopt of the SAME path reaches `startEmitter` again. Also reds `lazy:a-flush-after-an-adopt-does-not-start-a-second`.
